newsitem.title: LATVIA: SHIPPING COMPANY SEES BETTER Q1, $20 MLN LOSS'97.
newsitem.headline: SHIPPING COMPANY SEES BETTER Q1, $20 MLN LOSS'97.

text.p: The Latvian Shipping Company sees a 1997 loss of $20 million after expenditure cuts and a complete change of its dry-cargo strategy, the Diena Bizness newspaper reported on Monday.
But the company's president Andris Klavinsh added that its Q1 results will be better than expected, the newspaper said.
The company, estimated to be the world's 19th largest shipping firm, earlier this year decided on a five-year strategy of cutting losses and returning to profit in 1998.
The company also plans to sell most of its dry-cargo fleet of seven ships, keeping one or two, and to earn some $10 million in doing so, Klavinsh was quoted as saying.
The money would be put into reserves ahead of summer repairs and for the possible building of a new ship, Klavinsh said.
Apart from the seven dry-cargo ships, the company controls 39 tankers and 24 refrigerated vessels.
The company is estimated to have made a loss of $25 million last year and $51 million the year before.
Its annual turnover is close to $300 million.
